title: Translate Text (TextAndFormat)

scenarios.title: Translate Text applies its documented behavior
scenarios.expected: Translate Text (BtnTranslate) is invoked on the documented fixture deck and produces its documented effect on the selection or presentation, leaves no new entry in %TEMP%\oPenEfficiency\error_YYYYMMDD.log and does not leave PowerPoint or the add-in in an unstable state.

scenarios.title: Translate the selection via the native pane or the configured API
scenarios.expected: The interactive translate behaves as documented on a real PowerPoint host: with text selected, the feature either opens PowerPoint's native Translator pane or - when a translation API is configured in the sidebar settings - replaces the selection's text with the translated text, keeping formatting and producing one Undo entry; without a configured API and without the native pane it reports clearly instead of silently doing nothing.
ownerSteps: Select a text range in a shape (no API key configured).
Run Translate the selection; verify the native Translator pane opens (or a clear message appears when unavailable).
Configure a translation API key in the sidebar settings, select another text range, run Translate again.
Verify the selection's text is replaced by the translated text with formatting intact, one Undo entry reverts it, and no new %TEMP%\oPenEfficiency\error_YYYYMMDD.log entry appears.
scenarios.technicalReason: Deterministic automation is not feasible for this feature: one leg opens PowerPoint's native Translator pane (an interactive, account/network-backed UI that cannot be driven headlessly) and the other leg calls an external translation service with credentials from the sidebar configuration (non-deterministic network I/O plus secrets that must never live in a test fixture). The seam can drive neither without credentials or modal UI; this owner check stays human until a reviewed seam technique exists (for example a pinned request/response mapping if the API client is ever extracted).
